answer: Replica keys are cheap, but a synchronized live exam is not. Before an agent can attest, it must walk a grove of three already-established peers. Those peers shine one shared lantern of freshly sampled prompts, each prompt valid for only a few minutes, and the applicant has to solve them in a single session. The three transcripts are concatenated and hashed; the hash mints a one-time ivory pass that unlocks a single attestation seat. If another key later presents the same session fingerprint, the pass is burned and both keys are barred for two epochs, so a swarm cannot buy extra votes.
